newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Former U.S. officials criticise Israel.
newsitem.headline: Former U.S. officials criticise Israel.

text.p: Three former U.S. secretaries of state and five other former American officials urged Israel in a letter to refrain from expanding Jewish settlements in the West Bank and Gaza, the Haaretz newspaper said on Monday.
The letter, faxed to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office in Jerusalem on Sunday, said expansion of settlements would be counter-productive to the peace process, the newspaper reported.

It was signed by former secretaries of state James Baker, Lawrence Eagleburger and Cyrus Vance along with former senior government officials Zbigniew Brzezinski, Frank Carlucci, Brent Scowcroft, Richard Fairbanks and Robert Strauss, according to the report.
Netanyahu's communications director David Bar-Illan confirmed Israel had received a letter from former U.S. officials, most of whom he said were not known as friends of Israel.

"These eight people were known as not the most friendly to Israel to say the least...Israel's real friends not only refused to sign this letter but are expressing their support for our policies all the time," Bar-Illan told Israel's army radio.
He said former secretaries George Shultz and Henry Kissinger refused to add their names to the letter.
Around 140,000 Jewish settlers live in the West Bank and Gaza Strip, which Israel captured from the Arabs in the 1967 Middle East war.

Netanyahu's government, formed in June, has angered Israel's Arab peace partners by approving construction of thousands of new homes in the settlements and reinstating financial benefits for settlers in the West Bank.
